function: Learns GN transmit power, scheduling, and UAV trajectory by DRL (RLA); ALO also learns the UAV receive beam from a codebook (pp. 3-4).
system: UAV with linear M=30 antenna array collects from K=20 single-antenna ground IoT nodes; 80 MHz, 50 m altitude, no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 2, 5).
method: Reinforcement learning: outer-loop fusion DQN (dueling, noisy, double, prioritized replay) with inner-loop SCA beamforming (RLA); ALO is fully DRL with beam codebook (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Custom simulated multipath channel: large-scale fading, array response, small-scale fading coefficients; no standard model, dataset, or measurement; distributions not given (p. 2).
test_conditions: Agent trained over episodes (Figs. 2-3); results swept over UAV antennas, GN power, and number of GNs, averaged over 10 simulations; training per point not stated (pp. 5-6).
baselines: ALO algorithm based on double DQN (DDQN), learned, and fixed beamforming selection (FBS), not described further; no optimization or heuristic baseline (p. 5).
metrics: Reward and sum data collection (SDC) volume versus episodes, SDC versus UAV antennas and GN power, energy efficiency, Jain fairness index, UAV trajectories (pp. 5-6).
complexity: Order of complexity stated for RLA, O(UN(L(KN)^3.5 log(1/eps) + ((2+K)G)^2 + ...)) (p. 4), and for ALO, O(UN((2+2K)G)^2 + ...) (p. 5); no runtime.
q1_support: p. 2: "denotes the large-scale fading coefficient"; the channel is a custom multipath model (array response times small-scale fading); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data is named anywhere.
q2_support: p. 5: "are the average values obtained from 10 simulations" for the sweeps of Figs. 4-7 (antennas, GN power, GNs); no agent trained in one configuration and tested in another is reported, and the action size depends on K (p. 4).
q3_support: p. 5: "double DQN (DDQN) and fixed beamforming selection (FBS)" are the only two benchmarks; FBS is never described, so no benchmark is stated to be non-learned (no SCA-only, heuristic, or random-trajectory scheme).
q4_support: p. 4: "complexity of the RLA algorithm is O(U N (L(KN)3.5 log"; p. 5: "the computational complexity of the ALO algorithm is O(U N ((2 + 2K)G)2".
q5_support: p. 5: "the number of GNs K is 20"; the simulation uses its own parameters, with no code or data link or DOI, and no public dataset.
notes: Eligibility: learned GN transmit power (and beam codebook in ALO) is physical layer in an aerial link, learned jointly with UAV trajectory and scheduling (p. 3), so the above_phy check passes; area 6. RLA beamforming is SCA, not learned (p. 4). FBS is only named (p. 5); a reader who takes it as a fixed non-learned scheme would grade q3 as 1 through DDQN plus FBS. Title on p. 1 matches the DOI. Table I (p. 3) is notation only; figures were checked as images (pp. 5-6).
